summary: Shigeki Kudo was a Buddhist studies scholar. He worked as an assistant at Kyoto University, an assistant professor at Shuchiin University, and an assistant professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1972–1973).

Shigeo Kamata (1927–2001) specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology, studying at Komazawa University (~1948–1951) and the University of Tokyo (~1953–1958). He served at Tokyo (~1961–2001; professor ~1972–1988), Aichi Gakuin University, Matsugaoka Bunko, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Shigeru Gorai (1908–1993) studied religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology at the University of Tokyo (~1928–1931) and Kyoto University (~1931–1934). He held posts at Koyasan University (~1948–1957), Otani University (~1957–1964), and Ryukoku University (attested 1962).

Shigeru Matsumoto (1933–2010) was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1957) and Harvard University (~1963–1968). He held academic posts at Tenri University (~1970–1989) and the University of the Sacred Heart (~1989–2004).

Shigetsu Sasaki (1882–1945) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the Tokyo Academy of Fine Arts and under disciple master Sokatsu Shaku (~1905–1919). In 1931, he founded the First Zen Institute of America.
Shili Xiong (1885–1968) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at the China Inner Learning College in 1920. He held an academic post at Peking University from 1923 to 1955.

Shin Fujinaga is an indology and philosophy scholar. He held an attested post at Hiroshima University in 1992 and served as an associate professor at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested 1998–2000).
Shin Kitada is an indologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held a post at the Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010).

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu (1889–1980) studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University (~1915–1918) under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami. He held posts at Ryukoku University (~1919–1949), Kyoto University (1935–1949), Hanazono University (~1949–1963), and Harvard University (1958).

Shin'ichi Yoshinaga (1957–2022) specialized in religious and Buddhist studies, studying at Kyoto University from around 1976 to 1985. He held an academic post at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College, from around 1988 to 2018.
Shindai Sekiguchi (1907–1986) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1928–1933). He later held professorships at Hanazono University and Taisho University (~1957–1978).

Shingen Takagi is an indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University under teachers including Gisho Nakano, Yusho Miyasaka, Ensho Kanakura, and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as assistant professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995) at Koyasan University.
Shingo Einoo is an indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau (~1976–1983). He held an assistant post at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1984–1989).

Shinichi Tsuda specialized in Buddhist studies, indology, and Tibetology, studying at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and completing a Ph.D. at ANU under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham. He held posts at the Eastern Institute and ICPBS.

Shinjo Hinonishi (1928–2004) worked in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He held posts at Koyasan University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and professor (attested 2008).

Shinjo Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar who studied at Columbia University and under teachers including Hajime Nakamura. He held posts at the Toyo Bunko, University of Tokyo, University at Buffalo, University of Tsukuba, and Taisho University.

Shinjo Suguro (1925–2004) studied Buddhist studies, indology, and philosophy at the University of Tokyo (~1945–1987). He served at Rissho University as vice director in 1980 and later as professor emeritus (attested 2009).
Shinkai Sugawara (1925–2018) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1945–1951). He later held a post at Waseda University from around 1960 to 1996.

Shinkan Murakami studied Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy at Tohoku University (~1958–1963, ~1978–1979) under teachers including Ensho Kanakura and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as professor at Tohoku University (attested 1982–2000) and at Seiwa Gakuen College (~1996–2003).

Shinko Mochizuki (1869–1948) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Togai Soga and at Bukkyo University. He served at Shukyo University, including as president (1914–1928), and at Taisho University as professor, dean, and president (1930–1932).
